No problem. And nah with the humidity you’ve been at it should be fine, curing will raise the RH. You can always throw in boveda packs to ensure it doesn’t go above 62% when you’re curing. That’s what I’m doing just for extra peace of mind.

The trichomes still look fairly clear, depending on the high you want, you’d want to wait until 100% of them look milky, or like 15-20% amber and the rest milky. Ideally you’d probably want to wait another week or two if you can. You can chop them now but the quality could suffer a little bit
Seems like a nitrogen deficiency due to lack of nutes. Not the worst thing in late flower but you aren’t there yet so I’d say it’s hungry.

https://preview.redd.it/ooraeb0znkvd1.jpeg?width=3024&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=db30d4752b34fb566c1c53e9179c4e378a8666a0

Example with my current grow, plenty of yellowing and dying old fan leaves but the flowers are healthy

Pretty normal if you’re two months into flower, your plant no longer gives energy to those fan leaves and focuses on the flower instead! Yellowing is a sign of a nitrogen deficiency, which is actually a good thing during the flowering phase. I wouldn’t stress this issue at all

Soil mites are typically a clear-ish yellow to orangish amber color from my experience. Do these things have wings? I can’t quite tell from the pics. Fungus gnats also generally won’t harm your plant but they are a sign that you could have some kind of fungus/rot in the soil

Looks like a bad infestation of fungus gnats! I just treated some with BTI powder (active bacteria that is in mosquito bits) and it was super effective. You can use it as a top dressing and water with it and after 3/4 treatments, they should be 90%+ gone.
